title: Phase diagram of a semiflexible magnetic polymer in three dimensions
authors: Linda Delimi, Arpan Dey, Jean-Charles Walter
abstract: We study a semiflexible magnetic polymer in which each monomer carries a two-state spin, giving rise to coupled conformational, stiffness, and magnetic degrees of freedom. The model provides a minimal representation of nucleoprotein complexes in vivo, in which DNA bending rigidity and bridging proteins must be simultaneously accommodated. We employ Monte Carlo simulations on a face-centered-cubic (FCC) lattice, complemented by a variational free-energy upper-bound approach, to characterize the zero-field phase diagram as a function of bending stiffness and temperature. At low stiffness, we identify a first-order transition combining coil-to-globule collapse with a ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic transition. At lower temperatures, an additional first-order transition separates the disordered globule from an ordered crystal characterized by nematic-like orientational order of the bond tangents. At high stiffness, the globule disappears, resulting in a direct first-order coil-to-crystal transition. These results demonstrate how chain stiffness and magnetic degrees of freedom couple to polymer conformation and reorganize the zero-field phase diagram. Our model connects the two limiting cases of flexible magnetic polymers and semiflexible homopolymers, the latter corresponding to the strong-field limit in which all spins are aligned.
summary: This work investigates the phase diagram of a semiflexible magnetic polymer, modeling systems like DNA complexes. By combining Monte Carlo simulations and variational theory, the authors map out how chain stiffness and magnetic interactions drive multiple first-order transitions between coil, globule, and crystal states. The results highlight the complex interplay between conformational entropy and magnetic ordering in soft matter systems.
main_problem: To characterize the zero-field phase diagram of a semiflexible magnetic polymer as a function of bending stiffness and temperature.
main_result: The phase diagram exhibits multiple first-order transitions, including coil-to-globule and globule-to-crystal transitions, demonstrating how stiffness and magnetic coupling reorganize the polymer's conformational landscape.
method: The study employs Monte Carlo simulations on an FCC lattice, complemented by a variational free-energy upper-bound approach to analyze the thermodynamic limits.
model_or_system: The model is a semiflexible magnetic polymer chain where each monomer has a two-state spin, coupling conformational energy (bending penalty $\kappa$) with magnetic interactions ($J$). It serves as a minimal representation of nucleoprotein complexes.
key_observables: Contact Density ($ho_c$), Magnetization ($\langle|m|angle$), Nematic Order Parameter ($S$), and the overall phase diagram structure.
important_parameters: Bending stiffness ($\kappa$), Temperature ($T$), and the ratio $K = \kappa/J$. The zero-field limit ($h=0$) is the primary focus.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the zero-field limit ($h=0$) and uses variational upper bounds for the crystalline phase, which assumes an ordered, maximally compact cylindrical bundle structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the polymer, the evolution of ground state structure with stiffness, and the construction of the crystalline upper bound using a cylindrical bundle.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hamiltonian, first characterizing the zero-field phase diagram using simulations, then deriving analytical upper bounds for the crystalline phase, and finally mapping out the sequence of transitions based on the competition between bending costs and magnetic/contact energies.
why_interesting: The coupling between magnetic degrees of freedom and polymer conformation provides a rich model for studying coupled order parameters and phase transitions, relevant to many-body systems in condensed matter theory.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic of the semiflexible magnetic polymer. Each monomer carries a spin σi = ±1. Spatially neighbouring spins interact with coupling J and couple to an external field h, while consecutive bond tangents ˆti and ˆti+1 incur a bending penalty controlled by the stiffness κ.

FIG. 3: Phase diagram of the semiflexible magnetic polymer at zero field for N = 600. The coil, globule, and crystal regimes are indicated in blue, pink, and green, respectively. Blue circles, green triangles, and black crosses correspond to the Co–G, G–Cr, and Co–Cr boundaries, respectively; open orange squares indicate the resolved peaks of CV . The dashed green line represents the indicative continuation of the crystalline boundary at low stiffness. The open diamond marks the triple point (K⋆, T ⋆). Configurations A–G illustrate representative conformations at the positions indicated by the open circles; monomers are colored according to their magnetic state, σ = −1 in blue and σ = +1 in...

FIG. 4: Distributions of the observables in the vicinity of the Co–G transition. Distributions of the energy per monomer E/N (a), the absolute magnetization |m| (b), and the squared radius of gyration R2 g (c), for N = 600 and T = 3.375 at K = 6, approaching the critical value from below. The normalized histograms are complemented by Gaussian kernel density estimates (KDE).

FIG. 5: Size dependence of the maxima of the response functions associated with the Co–G transition. Maximum of the heat capacity Cmax V (a), of the susceptibility associated with the contact density χmax ρc (b), and of the magnetic susceptibility χmax |m| (c), as a function of the chain length N, at K = 6, approaching from below. The circles represent the mean values obtained over the independent replicas, and the error bars their standard deviations. The dashed gray lines indicate the reference linear dependence Xmax ∝N.
